summary: Feature-parity of the mold's own surface: data room, syncs, alerts, schedules, rendering, system of record, chat persistence, gates, and the tenant-isolation rows that cannot be satisfied by a status code.
not_covered: The Playwright card/stickloop specs — the /preview routes they drive are absent from this snapshot (see the `test:cards` row).
Anything behind a signed-in session: these scripts run offline against the mold's own fixtures.
Performance, accessibility and viewport behaviour — the load, accessibility and responsiveness lanes own those.

checks.name: test:dataroom
checks.why: The data room (dm.md) read/write path is the service surface itself.

checks.name: test:syncs
checks.why: Connector syncs normalize interactions; 0 instead of 2 means an ingested account looks empty.

checks.name: test:alerts
checks.why: Alerts are computed from the customer corpus; the snapshot ships data/customers.json empty.

checks.name: test:schedules
checks.why: A schedule that cannot be parsed cannot be run, so recurring workflows silently stop.

checks.name: test:cron-match
checks.why: Cron matching decides whether a scheduled workflow fires at all.

checks.name: test:workbook-spec
checks.why: Workbook specs drive the generated artefacts handed to a customer.

checks.name: test:render
checks.why: Rendering is what the operator actually sees.

checks.name: test:sor
checks.why: The system of record is the multiplayer context; a wrong write is a wrong shared truth.

checks.name: test:browser-security
checks.why: The optional browser capability must not become an exfiltration path.

checks.name: test:workflow-leases
checks.why: Leases stop two runners executing the same workflow step twice.

checks.name: test:workflow-args
checks.why: Custom workflow builder arguments are user input reaching the agent.

checks.name: test:chat-persistence
checks.why: A dropped turn is a lost conversation.

checks.name: test:chat-turn-state
checks.why: Turn state drives what the operator is allowed to do next.

checks.name: test:chat-attachments
checks.why: Attachments cross the blob boundary.

checks.name: test:email-signin
checks.why: Sign-in plus org membership is the tenancy boundary at the front door.

checks.name: test:step-context
checks.why: Step context is what each agent step is allowed to see.

checks.name: check:gates
checks.why: The mold's own release gates.

checks.name: check:tenancy
checks.why: Static tenancy check over the query layer: an org-unscoped query is a leak waiting for traffic.

checks.name: test:cards
checks.why: The card and stickloop Playwright specs are the only browser-level functional coverage in the mold.

requires.else: Blocked by the snapshot, not by this app: tests/cards.spec.ts drives /preview/cards and /preview/stickloop, and app/preview does not exist in this mold. Refresh the mold from source per molds/mold_v1/MOLD.md, then re-run. It is deliberately NOT invoked: its Playwright webServer would start `npm run dev` on 0.0.0.0:3000 on a box with no firewall.

checks.name: rls
checks.why: Two rows a status code cannot satisfy: the app role must not be able to read another workspace's rows, and the RUNNING build's health body must not say BYPASSRLS.

requires.else: This app did not ask for tenant isolation (datastores.postgres.rls is "off"), so there is nothing to prove. Set it in state/application/{app_id}/datastores.json if it should be isolated.
Deploy it first, then re-run: python3 .claude/scripts/provision.py {app_id} --deploy
